title: A Metal Splinter While Grinding

patient.name: Mr Lim Ah Seng
patient.presenting_complaint: Felt something sharp hit the left eye while grinding metal; now has pain, tearing and reduced vision

history.hpc: Mr Lim was grinding metal without goggles when he felt a sharp pain in the left eye. He says: 'Something fly into my eye when I grinding just now, very pain and my vision blur, got something inside maybe.' He is anxious. A high-velocity metal fragment raises strong suspicion of a penetrating eye injury — a Category 1 emergency. He must not press on or rub the eye.
history.social_hx: Metal workshop worker; not wearing safety goggles at the time.

iop.left: do NOT measure (no pressure on a possibly ruptured globe)

examination_findings.anterior_segment: Left eye: possible entry wound; do not manipulate. Do not attempt to remove any embedded object.

investigations.front_line_action: Recognise a likely penetrating eye injury (PEI) from high-velocity metal — a Category 1 emergency. Apply a protective eye shield (not a pad with pressure), do NOT touch, press on, or attempt to remove any object, and do NOT measure IOP or instil drops. Alert the doctor immediately and keep the patient calm and nil by mouth in case surgery is needed.
investigations.va_distance: Gross VA only; avoid any pressure on the globe.

diagnosis: Suspected penetrating (open globe) eye injury from a metal fragment — a Category 1, sight-threatening emergency. The PSA competency is recognising it, protecting the eye with a shield, avoiding all pressure/manipulation, keeping the patient nil by mouth, and escalating immediately; assessment and surgery are the doctor's.

immediate: Recognise the high-velocity metal mechanism as a likely penetrating eye injury (Category 1)
Apply a protective shield over the eye — do NOT apply a pressure pad
Do NOT touch, press, rub, or attempt to remove any embedded fragment, and do NOT instil drops or measure IOP
Alert the doctor immediately and keep the patient calm
Keep the patient nil by mouth (NBM) in case urgent surgery is required
Document the mechanism, time of injury, that a shield was applied, and the escalation
follow_up: Doctor to assess for an open globe and arrange urgent imaging/surgery as needed
Tetanus status to be checked given the metal injury
Document on the triage/emergency record and ensure notes follow the patient
patient_education: Reassure him while explaining he must not rub or press the eye
Explain the shield protects the eye and that the doctor will see him urgently
Explain why he should not eat or drink for now (possible surgery)
Advise on safety goggles to prevent future injuries (once stable)
